verses.1: And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “Please tell us where we should sit before you. It’s a difficult place from where we can’t get up.”
verses.2: Let us go to the Jordan. There, we will take one man captive from there. Then we will have a place where we can sit down and rest there. He said, “Go.”
verses.3: And one of them said, “Go, and go with your servants.” And he said, “I will go.”
verses.4: And he went with them. They entered the valley, and they cut down the trees.
verses.5: And one of the pillars collapsed, and the iron object fell into the water. It cried out, “Ah! My Lord!”
verses.6: And the man of God said, “It has fallen.” Then he looked at the place where it had fallen. He planted a tree there, and he sent down water from above.
verses.7: And Horem said to him, “Take it.” Then he stretched out his hand and took it.
verses.8: And the king of Aram fought against Israel. He commanded his servants, “Let me set up my camp in a place where I can be safe.”
verses.9: And the man of God sent an envoy to the king of Israel, saying, “Keep this place safe, for it is the place where the Ramses was buried.”
verses.10: And the king of Israel sent someone to the place where the man of God had told him to go. He was warned there, and no one or nothing could get away from him there.
verses.11: And the king of Aram became angry at this matter. He called out to his servants and said, “Tell me, who among our people is the king of Israel?”
verses.12: And one of his servants said to him, “Lord, the prophet Elisha, who is in Israel, will speak to the king of Israel about what he will say in your bedchamber.”
verses.13: And he said, “Go and see what he is like. Then I will send for him and take him away.” And he reported to them, “Here he is in the field.”
verses.14: And Solomon sent horses, chariots, and magnificent troops. They came at night and attacked the city.
verses.15: And the servant of the Lord got up and went out. There was a herd of cattle that was moving around in the city. A horse and rider also appeared. The boy said to him, “Oh, my master, what should I do?”
verses.16: And he said, “Do not fear, for many have been taken away from us because of what they did.”
verses.17: Elisha prayed, and said, “Lord, please open my eyes so that I can see.” Then the Lord opened the boy’s eyes. And he saw that the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.
verses.18: And they came to him and prayed to Jehovah. Elisha said, “Please, let this people be destroyed by the waters.” And so, the waters destroyed those people, as Elisha had commanded.
verses.19: And Elisha said to them, “This is not the right path, nor is this the right city. Go with me, and I will take you to the man you are seeking.” Then he led them away.
verses.20: And it happened that Shomron came forward. Elisha said, “Lord, open their eyes so that they can see.” And the Lord opened their eyes, and they could see. And behold, inside of Shomron there was a place.
verses.21: And the king of Israel said to Elisha, “Look at them! They are like my own father!”
verses.22: And he said, “Do not destroy what you have lost in your battles. Instead, give them food and water so that they can eat, drink, and go back to their homes.”
verses.23: And they ate and drank, and then they went back to their homes. But the kings of Aram were still not ready to enter the land of Israel.
verses.24: And after that, Abimelech, the king of Arim, attacked all his camps. He then went up to Shechem and destroyed it.
verses.25: And there was a great famine in Shemron. Then, people suffered greatly there until they were reduced to nothing; their wealth and possessions were destroyed. In fact, they were reduced to nothing at all.
verses.26: And there was a king of Israel who went through the desert. Then a woman cried out to him, saying, “Save me, O king!”
verses.27: And He said, “O Jehovah, save me from the east or from the west.”
verses.28: And the king said to her, “What are you going to do?” But the woman replied, “I will give my child to you. Let us eat today, and then we will eat our own children tomorrow.”
verses.29: And she will destroy her son, and they will eat him. I said to her, “On the next day, give me your son, and we will eat him. Then she will hide her son.”
verses.30: And when the king heard what the woman said, he tore his clothes. He stepped out of the heat and saw the blood on his arms from the room.
verses.31: And he said, “May God do this for me. And may Eliezer, son of Japhthah, stand before Him that day.”
verses.32: Elisha sat in his house, with the elders sitting beside him. He sent someone ahead of him before the angel came to him. He said to the elders, “Look! The son of the murderer has come to take my head.” When the angel entered, they closed the door behind him. Then they locked the door. Soon after, the sound of footsteps could be heard coming from the doorway.
verses.33: Then he spoke with them. And behold, the angel descended to him and said, “Behold, this is the bad news from Jehovah: what shall I say to Jehovah now?”
